headline: Windy, rainy front hits Friday; a stronger windstorm is possible Saturday night, with more storms continuing into next week.
summary: As of Thursday evening, a strong front from the Pacific is moving in. Rain starts tonight and spreads across western Washington early Friday morning, with gusty winds. The windiest places are the coast, Whidbey and San Juan Islands, and the northern interior (including western Whatcom and Skagit counties), where winds of 20-30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph are possible. Wind Advisories are in effect there Friday: 1 AM to 1 PM on the Northern Washington Coast, 4 AM to 4 PM for Island County, western Skagit and northwestern Snohomish lowlands, western Whatcom lowlands and San Juan County, and 7 AM to 4 PM on the Grays Harbor County coast. Most of Friday's rain falls during the day, about one-half to three-quarters of an inch at most over the higher terrain and coast, and one-tenth to one-quarter of an inch in most other lowlands. Snow levels (the elevation where rain turns to snow) start around 5,000-6,000 feet and rise to about 9,000 feet Friday afternoon, so high-elevation snow is not a big concern. Saturday should be a relative lull with leftover clouds, some showers, and highs in the 60s in most lowlands. Another front arrives Saturday night with a new round of strong winds. The coast, islands, and northern interior will likely see advisory-level winds, and other spots along Puget Sound could too, but it is too early to decide on alerts. Winds ease quickly Sunday, with most breezy conditions ending by mid-morning. After a brief break Sunday night into Monday, more rain arrives Monday afternoon into Tuesday. Temperatures stay a few degrees above normal, with lows mostly in the mid 40s to around 50. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will soak the ground and raise river flows, which could matter with later storms. Confidence is fairly high for Friday's winds, lower for how widely Saturday night's winds spread, and lower for Wednesday, when computer models disagree on whether rain reaches at least the Olympic Peninsula. Gale Warnings and rough seas are in effect offshore, with rough to severe conditions possible on the Grays Harbor Bar starting Friday.
changes: Through the day, Saturday night's wind went from a 50 percent chance of 50 mph gusts on the coast and north interior to likely advisory-level winds, possibly extending to Puget Sound. Forecasters also added timing for next week: a brief break Sunday night into Monday, then rain Monday afternoon into Tuesday, with Wednesday uncertain.
